title: Best Jingle Composers (2026): How to Hire One for Your Brand
h1: Best Jingle and Audio Intro Creators
description: How to hire a jingle composer for ads, podcasts or videos: what the package should include, usage rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: A jingle or short audio intro makes your brand, podcast or channel recognizable by ear. It can be a sung tagline, a short melody or a sound logo. Jingles go wrong when the usage rights do not cover how you use them, the melody sounds like a famous tune, or the files do not work in your videos or ads. This guide helps you commission one you can use everywhere.

faq.q: What is the difference between a jingle and a sound logo?
faq.a: A jingle is usually a short song, often with your brand name or tagline sung. A sound logo, or sonic logo, is a very short melody or sound that works like an audio version of your logo.

faq.q: Where can I use the jingle?
faq.a: Only where the license allows. Radio, TV, online ads, podcasts and in-store use may need different rights. Agree on all your uses in writing.
Ask for them. Common versions include a full length, a short version and a very short sting, so the jingle fits ads, intros and transitions.

faq.q: Can the jingle include a singer?
faq.a: Yes. Ask whether vocals are included, the voice type, and whether the singer's performance is covered by the rights.

faq.q: How do I keep it original?
faq.a: Ask the composer to confirm the melody is original. Reference tracks should guide the mood, not be copied.
